full_judgment: 4. A second appeal was preferred against that Judgment-S.A. No. 220 of 1963 in whicha contention was raised for the first time that the transfer by Delaney Estate to the plaintiff under the kabala dated 1.8.59 was hit by section 9(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Section 9(1) put an embargo on transfer, without previous permission of the Government, by private sale or gift, of any interest in an estate, or tenure or transfer of any land in khas possession of a rent-receiver whose rent-receiving interests were acquired by a notification under section 3(1) of the S ate Acquisition and Tenancy Act. But since this question was not raised during the trial, or even before the lower appellate court, the plaintiff got no opportunity to adduce evidence whether the transfer was made with the required permission. The High Court Division therefore sent the case on remand for determination of this question only. But the plaintiff feeling aggrieved moved this Court and obtained leave to appeal from that order for remand contending that in view of subsequent amendments of section 9(1) the requirement of previous permission for transfer of any land not exceeding 10 bighas was done away with and consequently the transfer was perfectly valid.
